translations.text: This blessed father of ours John came from the land of Mesopotamia, from the region of Antioch.
Under the guidance of the Holy Spirit he came to this land of Kartli, near the holy capital city of Mtskheta.
This holy and God-clothed father became a monk in his own country, and he lived in all humility and ascetic struggle,
in fasting and vigil, and in tears and supplication to God, as it says: "Knock, and it will be opened to you; ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find."
This blessed man also found grace before God. He saw what was far off as if it were near, and he shone like a star,
and the mighty works and wonders that he performed through God, against many kinds and every sort of illness, multiplied.
But he left the place where he was living and went far off into the desert, because he was fleeing this vain glory. He found a cave in that desert and settled in it with his disciples.
For a long time no one knew that place. From time to time he would send one of the disciples to fetch food, and so he lived in hiding.
But God again revealed his servant, as it says: "Whoever humbles himself will be exalted."
When it became known where he was living, people brought the sick and the demon-possessed to him on stretchers, and all were healed by the power of God and by the prayers of our holy father John.
Many are the miracles that are recorded there.
Since he fled the honors of the world, he resolved to go off into exile, to a place where his fame was not heard.
As he was considering this, he said to his disciples: "I am going to a foreign land. You stay here and pray for me too."
But they said to him: "As the Lord lives, we will not let you go alone. We will come too, so that we may not be deprived of the spring
from which we drink through you. For you are the guide of our souls, and through your graces we hope for mercy from God."
So bound together were they by spiritual love.
They set out from their own land and, under the guidance of the Holy Spirit, came to the city of Mtskheta.
They went in and venerated the holy pillar, which God had raised up and not man,
for neither the skill of the craftsmen nor the king himself, with a multitude of countless people, had been able to raise it for three days.
They gave up and left, and took all their machines away with them, because they had lost hope.
But the cause of all good things, the enlightener and converter of the Georgians, our mother,
our apostle Nino, stood in prayer to God with fervent tears and asked for God's help to raise the pillar.
As she was praying in this way, a power came from on high: the pillar hung up in the air, about a cubit high, and stood there by divine power.
At dawn King Mirian and the people of the Georgians came, saw this wonderful and glorious sight, and were amazed.
Then it came down slowly until it was set firmly on its foundation, and all who saw it and heard of it glorified God.
And a great many people were converted and were baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
The holy father John arrived before this Life-giving Pillar.
And he raised his hands and lifted his eyes to heaven, and he shed tears and offered thanks to God.
And God showed him a mountain near Mtskheta, to the north of the Life-giving Cross, and told him to go up to the summit of that mountain.
And he crossed the Aragvi and went up to venerate the precious Cross.
And when they had prayed, he went up that mountain with his disciples. When he had looked around, he said to his disciples: "Here I will dwell, for this place pleases me."
God did this for these reasons. First, so that he would become an adornment to the churches and to the Georgian peoples round about. Second, he settled in that place for this reason,
because the pagans had built a tower there, and demons had firmly settled in it, and the pagans served them with the smoke of sacrifices,
and so that now, through the prayer of that holy elder, God might sanctify that place.
When this God-clad father of ours, holy John, had gone up the mountain, he began to pray and make supplication to God, and he mightily endured all the assaults of the demons.
But he wished to live in solitude, and he said to his disciples: "Children, why do you stand idle?
Do you not know that my Lord Jesus Christ sent us forth and led us here for the benefit of this land?
For this land is a new planting. Therefore it is fitting that each of you go out and strengthen the brethren who have confessed Christ.
And love nothing more than God, brothers. Keep away from pleasure and gluttony, for that disobedience of Adam was born of pleasure and food, and it has remained upon his offspring.
This is what drove him out of paradise. If he had kept that commandment of fasting, corruption and death would not have gained dominion over us,
although now, through the incarnation of Christ, those of us who have now kept his commandment become incorruptible.
As for wine, even to speak of it is superfluous, for it is not for monks, since the apostle Paul called it the root and agent of wickedness:
"And do not get drunk with wine, in which there is debauchery."
It is a deadly poison and the mother of evil desires. Do not touch it at all, for it lures [?] us into eternal punishment.
My brothers, always remember death and where we are going. For this body is mortal and passing away, but the soul is forever immortal.
Let us struggle here and now for our souls, for all this life belongs to affliction, but the eternal life belongs to rest.
Let us be on guard for that terrible hour when the soul is separated from the body. For great is the fear when they lead the soul away and render to it the recompense of its deeds."
John taught his disciples much of this and of such things, and he said to them: "Go and strengthen the flocks of Christ."
And he sent some of them to Kakheti, some to Kukheti, and others to the upper country. He sent the blessed David to the desert of Gareja, and others to the area around our city.
And they went and settled, some in forests and some in caves and holes in the ground.
And Isidore went to the city of Samtavisi. In this way they separated from one another and lived as recluses, as was pleasing to the Holy Spirit.
Believers in Christ would come to those holy elders, and having been instructed by them and built up in spirit, they would go back to their own homes.
And they worked great healings with God's help and strengthened the faithful.
Now the holy father John had brought from his own country relics of the holy martyrs.
And when he sent out his disciples, he gave them some of those relics, so that by their grace they would be protected from all the snares of the devil.
He also kept some with himself, so that he could always look upon them, and in his mind be martyred together with them at all times, and have them as a comfort for soul and body.
He also had one disciple, by whom he was comforted. And his prayer rose up, purified the air, and passed through the ether.
But the demons, those haters of good, who had dwelt there from earlier times, could not bear the prayer of our father John, for it pierced them like arrows.
One day they rose up and fell upon the holy John, and began to fight him with many schemes of every kind.
They surrounded him, caused a disturbance, and said to him: "Who are you, and where are you from? For this place is ours.
And if you do not leave here, we will bring great and astonishing trials upon you."
But he sealed himself with the cross of Christ and said to them: "Here I am. And if you have received permission from Christ,
do whatever you wish, for I am a servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, and I am not afraid of your snares."
Then the chief of the demons called him by name: "John, John, why do you trouble us, and where did you come here from?
Now leave here, for this place is ours, and you cannot stay with us. And if you do not listen to me,
you will destroy yourself, for you cannot stand against this multitude that you see with us. Go away, and do not deceive yourself."
The holy John answered: "You never wish to plan any good for our race, for you are wicked, cunning, lying, and vain. So how could I listen to you?
I know all this thoroughly, that you do not wish good for people. And what is this place to you,
since the heavens and the earth were made by our God, and he created them as a resting place for us, his servants?!
But for you he has prepared the outer darkness and the unquenchable fire, in which you will be punished forever, you and all your helpers and all who follow your will.
Was it not you who took from us that paradise of delight? For you devised a scheme, drove our father Adam out of paradise, and by your trickery we were handed over to death.

But God, who is gentle and loves good, again showed mercy to the one created in his image. The one you had brought to dishonor and buried in the depths of hell, he raised up again in his mercy, brought him up on high, and granted him the kingdom.
And what you deceitfully promised him when you told him, 'You will be given divinity,' we have now received through our Lord Jesus Christ.
And now, see, you are driven out on every side by the children of Adam, and there is no place for you except that outer darkness, for you yourself hated the light and loved the darkness."
For you were an angel, and you became a rebel and fell because of your wickedness. Now, by the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, flee from this mountain, for Christ has granted me this.
When holy John had said all this, all those demons let out a cry of lamentation and woe and said:
"For by the calling on of the name of Jesus we are driven out of every place, and he gives power to all who follow him.
Woe, woe! Let us go to the innermost lands of the pagans and settle there."
And at once they came out of that mountain like a thick mist, headed toward the north, and vanished.
When all who lived around that mountain heard what God had done through the prayer of our holy father John, they all gave glory to God,
for they knew the wickedness of those demons who had dwelt on that mountain. And they said: "Truly God does the will of those who fear him."
The blessed elder lived on that mountain and strove to store up good works, so that he would not come before his Lord empty-handed.
And he began strict fasting and prayer, so that he might offer good works to the Lord.
At first that mountain had no water, and holy John saw the hard labours and sweat of his disciple, who carried water up from the foot of the mountain and brought it to the elder for his use.
He took pity on him and entreated God with tears to make water spring up on that high ridge.
And he who long ago gave water to the Israelites in the wilderness through his servant Moses, when waters sprang from the dry rock and satisfied the twelve tribes,
that same good God heard the entreaty of the holy elder and made sweet, cool water spring up from the dry ground on that mountain,
which flows to this day, to the glory of God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
When this miracle took place, it was spread abroad by those who lived around that mountain, for they all knew
that there had been no water at all on that mountain. For this reason people came from every side and brought the sick, and when they drank and anointed themselves,
they were all healed. And those who come with faith still receive benefit to this day.
But he did not wish to build on that place. He chose instead to live alone, for he found a small cave there, and in it he completed his life as a stranger in the world.
He lived afflicted and ill-treated, a man of whom this world was not worthy. And by his deeds he shone forth like the morning star.
News of him spread through the land of Kartli, for it is not possible that one who has lit a lamp should put it under a bushel; he puts it on a lampstand, so that it may give light to people.
Although he wished to hide himself, he still could not stay hidden. It was as when a perfumer fills a flask with ointment, puts it in another vessel, seals it, and thinks he has hidden it,
yet those who come near smell the fragrance of the ointment. In this way God glorified him, and God was glorified through him.
One day his disciple went to that spring to fetch water, and a large bear was standing over it.
He was afraid, turned back, and told the elder. The elder went and said to the bear: "If you have not drunk, drink and go away, and I tell you:
"From now on do not harm anyone among men when a man meets you on this mountain." And so it has been until now: the bear harms no one at all.
And when the elder had said this to the bear, it obeyed him like a servant, and went away with its head bowed, quietly.
Brothers, you who hear this, consider now the wonder and glory of God.
For just as once, long ago, Daniel tamed the beasts in the pit because of his fasting, which he kept for the sake of the divine law,
and did not touch the food of the Chaldeans at all, so too, through the prayer of this holy father of ours, the beasts of his mountain became gentle and harmless.
But I am ashamed of this: a beastly and speechless nature heard his words, and now their offspring, and their offspring's offspring, carry out the command of the holy father John,

while we have shown ourselves worse than wild beasts and dumb animals. For day after day we read aloud the things that happened, and we hear the commandments that were given, and yet we do not stop harming our neighbours.
We abstain from eating meat, yet we gnaw the flesh of our neighbours. We have received the commandment
that we should love one another, but we have neglected that command of the Lord. Know, then, that we are liable to judgment.

Let us take heed from now on, my brothers. Let us take heed and cast away from us envy and quarrelsomeness and plotting evil against our neighbour. Let us root out every wickedness and live in a way pleasing to God, so that we may not be condemned forever.
But I will return to my earlier account.
Once they brought to this holy father of ours, John, a man on a bed who was bent over and paralysed.
All his limbs had gone slack. They brought him in before him and pleaded with holy John:
"Have mercy, holy one of God, on this paralysed man, for we believe that you are able to heal him by the power of Christ."
And the paralysed man himself cried out again: "Have mercy on me, servant of God, on this dead man who is not yet buried, and grant me a little grace, so that I may be healed."
Although this task seemed heavy to blessed John, he remembered the saying of Paul, who says:
"You who are strong, bear the weak." Therefore he said to him, "Our Lord Jesus Christ heals you."
At that very moment he stood up on his feet, and his slack limbs were quickly healed. Those who saw it gave thanks to God and to holy John.
Again they brought a man possessed by a demon, who was so badly tormented that he could not even speak. John saw him and had pity on him.
Holy John answered and said: "Wicked spirit, why do you torment this man? The desert and waterless place has been given to you.
"I tell you in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: come out of this man." And at his very command it came out.
And the man was healed, and everyone marveled. And the elder said this to them: "Why are you amazed? For I am not a healer,
but by calling on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ every disease and every power of darkness flees, for he himself declared,
'Whoever believes in me will also do what I do, and he will do greater things than mine.'"
These few out of his many great deeds we have written down, so as not to draw out the time too long. But they are enough to give a taste of that God-clothed man.
Just as a single bucket shows what the water of a great river tastes like, so it is with blessed John, for those who wish [to know him].
Many are the miracles that our holy father John performed.
But now let us speak of his blessed disciples, who were enlightened by divine grace, enlightened others as well, and built monasteries,
which still stand to this day, and in which healings take place. We are not able to tell of each of them one by one.
One of the disciples, named Tata, built a monastery below, at the foot of that mountain. In it the monks increased in number and lived in complete good order.
We will remember the others later, and let us glorify God, to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
Our blessed father John grew old in that cave and completed his course with many struggles.
And he began to grow weak.
He called some of his disciples, and Tata, who was [?] below that mountain, and Elias the deacon, and said to them:

"My children, the hour of my end has come, and I am going to my Lord. I am greatly afraid of the guardians of the air, for they are terrifying and hold back souls so that they may not go up to the Kingdom of Heaven.
"You too should expect this, my beloved children. Guard yourselves now, and pray for me.
"And who else could save us from their hands except God, who sent his Son,
"our Lord Jesus Christ? And he set us free from death and from every harm of the devil, but only those
"who follow him with a fervent heart and serve him in holiness. For this reason I beg you that we live in holiness and righteousness."
He instructed them to lay his body in that same place where he had lived as a stranger [i.e. as an ascetic].
He received the Holy Mysteries, raised his eyes, and with a joyful face looked at certain ones who had come to comfort him.
He turned his eyes toward them as toward friends, gave up his spirit, and committed it to the Lord.
And Jacob's ladder was seen here too, and the angels of God were coming down, and the Lord stood firmly at the top of the ladder, and he said to him,
"I am the God of Abraham your father"; now come to me, so that I may give you rest from your labors. In this way, brothers, God glorifies those who glorify him.
His disciples wept because the holy father had parted from them.
But they disregarded the elder's word, because the place where he had instructed them to lay his body seemed unworthy to them.
For priests and deacons and a crowd of people came, carried away the elder's relics, and laid them in the monastery of Tata,
his disciple. They made a precious reliquary and buried in it the holy body of our blessed father John.
His disciples wept and said: "Good father, why have you left us?"
"With whom shall we now see an angelic face? Who will heal the infirmity of men, raise up fallen minds, and be a medicine for those wounded by demons,
or who will water our villages with holy tears?" And so they went away weeping.
But holy John did not let his word be disregarded. Where he had found grace in solitude, and so that we might see and believe
that even after death he is alive and has boldness before God, for this reason he wished his relics to be laid in that very place.
And in the place where his body had been laid, severe earthquakes occurred, and the people of that place were afflicted.
They remembered the elder's command and understood that the earthquakes were happening because of it. So they informed the chief of the fathers.
He was astonished and went with priests and deacons, and with great honour they carried him up to his own place and laid his relics there in the same coffin.
And after that they built a church.
After he was carried up, the earthquakes ceased, and many other miracles also took place by the will of Christ and the grace of holy John.
For many who were sick, crippled or possessed by demons were healed when he was carried up, and all who saw it glorified God.
And if anyone comes to him with faith, healings take place through him even now.
After a long time, the holy Catholicos Clement built another church on the east side of the church, in the name of the holy Baptist, for the glorification of the holy consubstantial Trinity.
One of the disciples of this blessed John built Alaverdi, from which great wonders come forth to this very day.
Another built the cave of Iulta [?], and others built monasteries in Kakheti.
David built the desert of Gareja and spent a long time there with a dragon.
At last he gave a command and drove that nest of demons out of the place. He also performed many other miracles.
Another built a monastery above the village, which no female can enter and where no bird can nest.
We cannot mention them all. Holy Ise became bishop of Tsilkani, and the tomb of that blessed man can still be seen today.
